name: Depth Consistency
description: Compares monocular depth estimates across consecutive frames to identify sudden depth discontinuities and physically implausible 3D structure changes that reveal AI-synthesized scene geometry.
mechanism:
This method analyzes depth consistency across video frames for deepfake and manipulation detection:

1. **Monocular Depth Estimation**: Per-frame relative depth maps are estimated using monocular depth cues: texture gradients, defocus, atmospheric perspective, relative size, and occlusion relationships. Each pixel receives a relative depth value consistent with the scene geometry.

2. **Temporal Depth Stability**: Depth maps across consecutive frames should show smooth, physically motivated changes. The method tracks depth map evolution — natural scene depth changes are caused by camera motion (smooth, globally coherent) or object motion (local, bounded). Deepfakes may produce temporally unstable depth maps, especially at face-swap boundaries where generated face depth differs from the original face geometry.

3. **Face-Scene Depth Integration**: The depth relationship between the face and surrounding scene must be consistent. The method checks: (a) face depth varies correctly with camera distance, (b) face depth matches nearby objects at similar distances, (c) face depth changes are consistent with measured face scale changes. Composited deepfake faces may show depth inconsistencies with the scene.

4. **Depth-Defocus Consistency**: Estimated depth should correlate with defocus blur — objects at similar depths should show similar focus. The method cross-validates depth estimates against local defocus measures. AI-generated faces may show incorrect depth-defocus relationships, appearing sharp at depths where the background is blurred (or vice versa).

5. **3D Geometric Consistency Scoring**: The implied 3D geometry is checked for physical plausibility. Face orientation (from landmarks) should produce consistent depth gradients. Perspective distortion should match the estimated camera parameters. Violations of geometric consistency indicate manipulation, yielding an elevated forensic score.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through depth consistency analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video
